name: VUE
aliases: Vault or Uterine prolapse surgery Evaluation
question: Does uterine preservation differ from vaginal hysterectomy for uterine prolapse, and abdominal from vaginal vault suspension for vault prolapse, in symptoms, safety and cost?

design.blinding: Outcome assessors blinded; surgeons not blinded; participants unblinded on request
design.population: Women at UK hospitals having surgery for uterine prolapse (565 randomized) or for vault prolapse after hysterectomy (209 randomized).
design.description: Two parallel pragmatic multicenter randomized surgical trials (uterine and vault)
design.locator: HTA report p. 27, Figure 2; p. 57, Figure 8; pp. 5-9

verdictNote: No 12-month symptom difference in either trial; vault trial interval was wider (−2.08 to 0.86).
takeaway: In two parallel UK trials, uterine preservation did not differ from vaginal hysterectomy (563 women analyzed) and abdominal did not differ from vaginal vault suspension (208) in 12-month Pelvic Organ Prolapse Symptom Score or serious adverse events; abdominal repair cost £570 more.

reports.label: 12-month report (HTA monograph)
reports.dateLocator: Crossref and PubMed give March 2020 only
reports.citation: Hemming C, Constable L, Goulao B, et al. Surgical interventions for uterine prolapse and for vault prolapse: the two VUE RCTs. *Health Technol Assess.* 2020;24(13):1-220. doi:10.3310/hta24130
reports.followUp: 12 months after randomization (symptoms, quality of life) and 12 months after surgery (POP-Q examination)

results.measure: 12-month Pelvic Organ Prolapse Symptom Score (0 to 28; lower is better), uterine trial; adjusted mean difference (uterine preservation minus vaginal hysterectomy)
results.note: The trial was sized to detect a 2-point difference (0.28 SD); the interval excludes it. Baseline scores were 13.7 and 13.5.

results.endpoint: Prolapse-related quality of life, uterine trial
results.measure: 12-month prolapse-related quality of life (0 to 10 visual analogue scale; lower is better), uterine trial; adjusted mean difference
12-month incremental NHS cost, multiply imputed base case, 2015–16 pounds sterling (uterine preservation minus vaginal hysterectomy)
results.locator: HTA report pp. 43-44, Table 18; p. 47; p. xxxii
results.note: Adjusted QALY difference −0.004 (95% CI −0.026 to 0.019): uterine preservation was dominated by vaginal hysterectomy, with a 15% probability of cost-effectiveness at £30,000 per QALY. With hospital tariff costing for the operation the probability was 85%.

results.endpoint: Overall prolapse stage 2b or more, uterine trial
results.measure: POP-Q overall stage 2b or more 12 months after surgery, uterine trial; adjusted odds ratio

results.endpoint: Apical stage 2b or more, uterine trial
results.measure: POP-Q apical stage 2b or more 12 months after surgery, uterine trial; adjusted odds ratio
results.locator: HTA report p. 33, Table 11; p. 22, Table 4; p. 25
results.note: Baseline apical stage 2b or more was 137/280 (48.9%) versus 164/283 (58.0%); 28.2% of women had apical stage 0 or 1.

results.measure: Further prolapse surgery within 12 months of surgery, uterine trial; adjusted odds ratio
results.note: Women readmitted for further surgery in the first 12 months: 18/244 (7.4%) versus 11/242 (4.5%).

results.measure: Further apical surgery within 12 months of surgery, uterine trial; adjusted odds ratio
Further anterior repair within 12 months of surgery, uterine trial; adjusted odds ratio

results.endpoint: Would recommend to a friend, uterine trial
results.measure: Would recommend the operation to a friend 12 months after randomization, uterine trial; adjusted odds ratio
results.note: Prolapse reported better than a year earlier: 208/229 (90.8%) versus 221/232 (95.3%; OR 0.49, 95% CI 0.22 to 1.05). Completely or fairly satisfied: 196/229 (85.6%) versus 211/233 (90.6%; OR 0.62, 95% CI 0.34 to 1.13).

results.measure: Urgency at 12 months after randomization, uterine trial; adjusted odds ratio
results.note: The text calls this urge incontinence; the table row is labeled urgency. Any incontinence: 87/237 (36.7%) versus 84/241 (34.9%); de novo incontinence 44/172 (25.6%) versus 44/168 (26.2%).

results.measure: Severe fecal incontinence at 12 months after randomization, uterine trial; adjusted odds ratio
results.note: Small numbers; fecal incontinence of any frequency was 59/227 (26.0%) versus 61/235 (26.0%).

results.endpoint: Sensitivity analyses of POP-SS, uterine trial
results.measure: 12-month POP-SS, uterine trial; adjusted mean difference (uterine preservation minus vaginal hysterectomy)
results.note: Multiple imputation of missing primary outcomes gave −0.02 (95% CI −0.83 to 0.78); the per-protocol analysis of women who received the allocated operation gave 0.19 (95% CI −0.70 to 1.08; P=0.68).

results.measure: Women having intercourse 12 months after randomization, uterine trial
results.note: Vaginal and sexual symptom scores and quality-of-life scores did not differ significantly; the ICI Sexual Matters score was 7.8 versus 8.7 (adjusted difference −2.47, 95% CI −6.78 to 1.85).

results.measure: 12-month Pelvic Organ Prolapse Symptom Score (0 to 28; lower is better), vault trial; adjusted mean difference (abdominal minus vaginal)
results.note: Sample size was revised to a projected 280 women (80% power for 2.5 points); 209 were randomized and 208 analyzed after one post-randomization exclusion. Baseline scores were 15.1 and 14.8.

results.endpoint: Prolapse-related quality of life, vault trial
results.measure: 12-month prolapse-related quality of life (0 to 10 visual analogue scale; lower is better), vault trial; adjusted mean difference
12-month incremental NHS cost, multiply imputed base case, 2015–16 pounds sterling (abdominal minus vaginal)
results.locator: HTA report p. 72, Table 35; p. 75; p. xxxii
results.note: Adjusted QALY difference 0.004 (95% CI −0.031 to 0.041); abdominal repair had a 17% probability of cost-effectiveness at £30,000 per QALY.

results.endpoint: Overall prolapse stage 2b or more, vault trial
results.measure: POP-Q overall stage 2b or more 12 months after surgery, vault trial; adjusted odds ratio

results.endpoint: Apical stage 2b or more, vault trial
results.measure: POP-Q vault (apical) stage 2b or more 12 months after surgery, vault trial; adjusted odds ratio
results.note: Baseline objective vault prolapse (stage 2b or more) was 39.4%.

results.endpoint: Anterior stage 2b or more, vault trial
results.measure: POP-Q anterior stage 2b or more 12 months after surgery, vault trial; adjusted odds ratio
results.note: Vaginal repair more often included a concomitant anterior or posterior repair (76.0% versus 34.7%).

results.measure: Further prolapse surgery within 12 months of surgery, vault trial; adjusted odds ratio
Further apical surgery within 12 months of surgery, vault trial; adjusted odds ratio

results.endpoint: Sensitivity analyses of POP-SS, vault trial
results.measure: 12-month POP-SS, vault trial; adjusted mean difference (abdominal minus vaginal)
results.note: Multiple imputation of missing primary outcomes gave −0.32 (95% CI −1.71 to 1.06); the per-protocol analysis gave −0.99 (95% CI −2.59 to 0.60; P=0.22).

harms.label: Serious related adverse events, uterine trial
harms.note: Within 12 months of surgery, among women who had surgery (N=262 and 269); effect 0.82 (95% CI 0.38 to 1.75; P=0.60). Hospitalization was the most common type (10 versus 9).

harms.label: Serious related adverse events, vault trial
harms.note: Within 12 months of surgery (N=102 and 100); odds ratio 0.97 (95% CI 0.27 to 3.44; P=0.96).

harms.label: Mesh exposure requiring surgery, both trials
harms.note: Two exposures among 235 mesh procedures (0.9%) in the first 12 months, both treated by surgical removal. One followed an apical procedure in the uterine trial (1 of 129 apical or concomitant mesh procedures) and one followed a concomitant tension-free vaginal tape in the vault trial (1 of 106).

harms.label: Excessive blood loss (over 500 mL), serious event, uterine trial
harms.note: Blood transfusion occurred in 0 versus 1 (0.4%) women and blood vessel injury in 0 versus 1 (0.4%). Postoperative serious events included urinary retention or voiding difficulty needing conservative treatment in 5 (2.0%) versus 1 (0.4%).

harms.label: Non-serious related adverse events, uterine trial
Bladder or bowel injury, serious intraoperative event, vault trial
harms.note: Postoperative serious events also included catheterization for more than 10 days (0 versus 1), perineal scarring or tightness needing surgery (0 versus 1) and vaginal adhesions (0 versus 1).

harms.label: Non-serious related adverse events, vault trial

values.vaginal: blood loss mean 107.8 mL (SD 74.8; n=86); stay mean 1.8 days (SD 1.2; n=100)

relations.note: The same group's earlier trial; its methods, outcome measures and symptom-score standard deviation informed VUE's design and sample size.
Same uterine-preservation question; SAVE-U's sacrospinous hysteropexy was also noninferior to vaginal hysterectomy at 12 months.
Same question with a mesh hysteropexy; SUPeR also found no significant reduction in composite failure versus vaginal hysterectomy at 36 months.
Same vault question; ASPIRe's 36-month composite failure favored sacrocolpopexy, while VUE's 12-month symptom score did not differ.
